prompt: Why does the lesson say structural decisions outlive technologies?
hint: Swap the broker for another product and see what stays.

choices.text: Because technologies are chosen by teams and structure by the architect
choices.why: Both kinds are taken by teams most of the time; the lesson's point is about what survives a change.

choices.text: Replacing a product leaves the shape of the system standing
choices.why: Right: Payments would still learn of proofs asynchronously, with every consequence of that.

choices.text: Because structure is drawn on diagrams and technology is not
choices.why: A drawing is not the decision, as the section's last part says.

choices.text: Because a structure, once chosen, is frozen
choices.why: Structures change too; they cost more to change than a library.

prompt: A pull request adds one query from Pricing straight into the monolith's deliveries table. What kind of decision is it making, by the lesson?
hint: Five kinds of structural decision; one of them Carreto got wrong for longest.

choices.text: A layering decision inside Pricing
choices.why: It reaches outside Pricing into another system's data.

choices.text: A technology decision about the database
choices.why: The database stays the same; who reads it changes.

choices.text: None: one query is too small to be a decision
choices.why: Five writers accumulated one small change at a time; that is the lesson's warning.

choices.text: A decision about who owns the data
choices.why: Right: it makes Pricing depend on a table it does not own, whether its author meant to or not.

prompt: Which of these make a decision architectural, by Renata's three tests? Choose all that apply.
hint: Any one of the three is enough.

choices.text: It is expensive to reverse
choices.why: Yes: the first test, from Booch's cost of change.

choices.text: It uses a technology new to the company
choices.why: Novelty is not one of the tests; a new library inside one team stays the team's.

choices.text: Its consequences land on another team
choices.why: Yes: crossing a team boundary is the second test.

choices.text: It sets how available a shared service will be
choices.why: Yes: a system-wide quality attribute is the third test.

prompt: Which test framework the Matching team uses: who decides, by the lesson's table?
hint: Cheap to reverse, inside one team.

choices.text: Renata, so the seven teams stay consistent
choices.why: Consistency of test tools passes none of the three tests.

choices.text: The architecture forum
choices.why: The forum is for decisions that cross teams.

choices.text: The Matching team
choices.why: Right: and an architect reaching for it is in the way.

choices.text: Platform, because it runs CI
choices.why: Running the pipeline does not make Platform the owner of Matching's tests.

prompt: For a week after ANTT published a new floor table, Pricing and the Shipper app disagreed about the minimum freight. What structural lesson does the course draw?
hint: Where a rule lives.

choices.text: A rule with two homes is two rules, and they drift
choices.why: Right: the rule belongs in Pricing alone, and others ask Pricing.

choices.text: The Shipper app should load the ANTT table as well
choices.why: That keeps two homes and adds a second loader to keep in step.

choices.text: Regulatory checks belong in the front end, closest to the user
choices.why: The copy in the front end was the stale one.

choices.text: Pricing should have notified Shipper by e-mail
choices.why: A notice is a habit; a single owner is a structure.

prompt: Renata sees a pull request that would make Pricing a second writer of the deliveries table. What does she do, by the lesson?
hint: Not to approve, but to recognise.

choices.text: Blocks it until the architecture forum meets next month
choices.why: She does not block; that would make her a gate.

choices.text: Approves it, since teams own their code
choices.why: The change reaches into data Pricing does not own, so it is more than Pricing's code.

choices.text: Names the decision and leaves it with the team
choices.why: Right: the decision stops being silent, and stays with the team.

choices.text: Rewrites it to use an event instead
choices.why: Rewriting another team's change takes the decision away from them.

prompt: Why can "Payments must be reliable" not settle a design decision?
hint: Two engineers can agree with it and build opposite systems.

choices.text: Reliability is not a quality attribute
choices.why: It is one; the problem is the missing numbers.

choices.text: It names no event, condition or measure
choices.why: Right: never down, never wrong, never late? It does not say.

choices.text: Payments is too small for reliability to matter
choices.why: Reliability of payouts is central to the 24-hour promise.

choices.text: Only the bank partner decides how reliable Payments is
choices.why: Payments' response to a bank failure is exactly what the scenario designs.

prompt: Put the six parts of a quality attribute scenario in the order the lesson's figure draws them.
hint: Who causes it comes first; how you would know comes last.
trap: Putting the response measure early tempts you to write it before knowing what is being measured.

prompt: Which part of the scenario turns "payouts are retried" from an opinion into a test?
hint: Without it, one retry a day would satisfy the sentence.

choices.text: The environment it happens in
choices.why: It says when, not how well.

choices.text: The source of the event
choices.why: It says who causes the event.

choices.text: The artefact that receives it
choices.why: It says which part of the system receives the event.

choices.text: The response measure
choices.why: Right: within 2 hours of recovery, zero duplicates; something a design is checked against.

prompt: Match each part of Pricing's modifiability scenario to its content.
hint: The table arrives, and two working days later it is live.

pairs.right: the floor stage of the quote
live within two working days, code changed only in the floor module

right_distractors: the shipper who posts the load

prompt: Why is the shipper's contest window a trade-off point in the ATAM sense?
hint: One decision, two scenarios, opposite directions.

choices.text: Because it involves the bank partner
choices.why: The bank partner plays no part in the window's length.

choices.text: Because it is a technical setting nobody outside Payments sees
choices.why: It is a business setting, owned by Helena and Sílvio on either side.

choices.text: Its length pulls two measures in opposite directions
choices.why: Right: shorter pays drivers sooner and protects Carreto less.

choices.text: Because ANTT sets its length by regulation
choices.why: The 12 hours were Sílvio's condition, not a regulation.

prompt: More retries improve the availability scenario and threaten "none paid twice". What resolved that trade-off at Carreto?
hint: Record 7 requires it.

choices.text: Fewer retries, accepting some late payouts
choices.why: That gives up availability rather than protecting both.

choices.text: The delivery id as an idempotency key
choices.why: Right: a repeated payout changes nothing, so retries stop being dangerous.

choices.text: A second bank partner for Pix
choices.why: That addresses the partner being down, not duplicates.

choices.text: Finance reviewing every payout by hand
choices.why: That would break the 24-hour budget long before it caught a duplicate.

prompt: Why did Renata take "every invoice references its authorised CT-e" out of the weighted criteria?
hint: A legal requirement scored at 25% could be outvoted.

choices.text: Because all three options scored the same on it
choices.why: They did not need to; a constraint is applied before scoring, whatever the scores.

choices.text: It is a constraint, not a weight
choices.why: Right: it filters options before the matrix rather than trading against convenience.

choices.text: Because legal matters are for finance to decide
choices.why: Who owns the law is not the point; the point is that it is not weighable.

choices.text: To keep the matrix at five criteria
choices.why: The count of criteria is incidental.

prompt: In the invoicing matrix, set the weights to time 40% and team independence 10%, leaving running cost 15%, CT-e fit 25% and exit 10%. What is option B's weighted total? B scores 2, 5, 2, 4 and 4 on those criteria.
hint: Sum of weight times score.

prompt: Why should the weights be agreed before anyone scores the options?
hint: What happens to weights set after the favourite is known?

choices.text: Late weights get tuned until the favourite wins
choices.why: Right: the matrix then confirms a preference instead of testing it.

choices.text: Scoring is faster once weights are fixed
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: Weights decide the scale of the scores
choices.why: Scores are 1 to 5 regardless of weights.

choices.text: The architect sets the weights and the team the scores
choices.why: In the lesson the owners set the weights, and Renata set neither.

prompt: The sensitivity check found A and B cross at 32.5% weight on team independence. What does the lesson say that tells the team?
hint: Which argument is worth having.

choices.text: That A is the right answer with 4.05 points
choices.why: The point is how fragile that margin is.

choices.text: That the matrix is useless and should be dropped
choices.why: It did its job: it found the one number to argue about.

choices.text: One weight decides it, so settle that weight
choices.why: Right: is independence worth a third of the decision? The other weights do not change the winner.

choices.text: That C should be dropped because it never moves
choices.why: C staying flat is a property of its scores, not a reason to drop it.

prompt: What did Renata own in the invoicing decision?
hint: Not the answer.

choices.text: The final choice, as the company's architect
choices.why: Tomás decided, with Bruno and Helena on either side.

choices.text: The scores, since she knows every system
choices.why: She scored nothing herself.

choices.text: The method
choices.why: Right: constraint first, weights before scores, the sensitivity check, the crossover in front of the owners.

choices.text: The weights, to keep them neutral
choices.why: The weights came from the people who own each criterion.

prompt: The finance analyst's spreadsheet lost to the three options. Why does the lesson still put "do nothing" on the list?
hint: Lesson 14 makes it a habit.

choices.text: To make the matrix look balanced to finance
choices.why: Appearances are not the reason.

choices.text: It is a real option, with costs of its own
choices.why: Right: it lost because volume outgrew one person, and that had to be shown, not assumed.

choices.text: Because the analyst asked for it to be included
choices.why: Who asked is not the argument.

choices.text: Because a matrix needs at least four options to work
choices.why: Three options are enough for a matrix.

prompt: Booch: architecture is the set of significant design decisions, where significance is measured by the cost of ___.
hint: Lesson 1's definition, used here as the first test.

prompt: Matching wants to offer each new load to five drivers at once to fill loads faster. Which quality attributes trade against each other here?
hint: Two drivers, one warehouse, one load.

choices.text: Security against usability for drivers
choices.why: Nothing about access or logins is at stake.

choices.text: Cost against modifiability
choices.why: The question is about outcomes for drivers, not about code changes.

choices.text: Performance against modifiability
choices.why: That pair is the bank adapter's.

choices.text: Speed of offers against consistency
choices.why: Right: faster offers risk two drivers accepting the same load.

prompt: Match each Carreto decision to who decides it, by the lesson's table.
hint: Expensive to reverse? Crosses teams?

pairs.left: the fields of the DeliveryProved event

prompt: Shipper invoicing went into the monolith, behind an interface. What makes the team revisit that, by the decision record?
hint: The record carries a condition for changing course.

choices.text: Any new quarter
choices.why: A calendar is not the condition written down.

choices.text: Bruno disagreeing again at the next architecture forum
choices.why: Disagreement alone reopens nothing; a changed context does.

choices.text: Changes held up weekly by the deploy schedule
choices.why: Right: more than one change a week blocked by the monolith's deploys; the crossover made observable.

choices.text: A higher score for option B in a new, rescored matrix
choices.why: Rescoring without a changed context is re-litigating.
